annotation_description: Gem25F Analyst skipped their land drop on turn 2 with two lands in hand (Mountain and Rockface Village). Missing a land drop is significant, especially when they have a hand full of spells that need mana - three Slickshot Show-Offs (each costing 1R), Lightning Helix (RW), and Nova Hellkite (3RR). Playing Mountain here would allow them to have 2 mana on turn 2, enabling a Slickshot Show-Off or Lightning Helix to kill Momo. Even if they wanted to hold up mana or sequence differently, there is no reason to skip a land drop entirely when you have lands in hand and expensive cards to cast.

Playing Rockface Village instead of Mountain means Sunbillow Verge cannot activate its red mana ability (requires controlling a Mountain or Plains). This locks the player out of casting Lightning Helix on turn 3 and constrains their mana flexibility going forward. Mountain would have unlocked Sunbillow Verge's dual-color capability immediately.

The player passed their turn without playing their Mountain (missing a land drop) and without casting or plotting any of their three Slickshot Show-Offs despite having the mana to do so. This wastes an entire turn of development on turn 2, falling behind against Momo which will grow as the opponent develops their board.

Casting Slickshot Show-Off in the precombat main phase rather than plotting it or waiting. With 3 lands and Slickshot having haste, casting it precombat is fine for attacking this turn. However, the opponent has Momo (1/1 flying) and Sarkhan (2/2) on board. The key question is whether casting Slickshot now versus plotting one (to deploy it for free next turn alongside noncreature spells) would be better. Casting precombat with a creature that has haste is generally correct since you want to attack. But with 3 Slickshot Show-Offs in hand, plotting one this turn (spending the same 1R) to set up a bigger burst turn next turn with multiple Slickshots + burn spells could be more explosive. That said, applying pressure now with the 1/2 flyer is reasonable, and plotting doesn't generate immediate board presence. The more notable consideration is whether to use Burst Lightning or Lightning Helix on Sarkhan first before combat, since Sarkhan could become a Dragon threat if the opponent plays Nova Hellkite or another Dragon. But overall, casting Slickshot precombat with haste to attack is defensible.

Slickshot Show-Off is a 1/2 flyer with haste that grows with noncreature spells. It's tapped and attacking, meaning the opponent already committed it. Sarkhan is a 2/2 that could block and kill the 1/2 Slickshot cleanly (assuming no pump spells). The opponent's lands are all tapped (Sunbillow Verge, Mountain, Rockface Village all tapped or one untapped), so there's limited ability to cast pump spells. Rockface Village is untapped but can only pump Lizard/Mouse/Otter/Raccoon types, not a Bird Wizard. The opponent has no untapped mana sources to cast instants like Burst Lightning or Lightning Helix to protect the Slickshot. Blocking with Sarkhan would be a clean kill on a dangerous threat with no risk given the opponent's tapped mana state.

Using Get Lost on a tapped Slickshot Show-Off while the opponent is tapped out gives them two Map tokens. The Show-Off is a real threat but can't attack this turn, and Vorthos could develop the board with Charming Prince (potentially scrying 2) while holding Get Lost for a more critical moment or a bigger threat like Nova Hellkite from the opponent's side.

message: Select a creature, enchantment, or planeswalker
annotation_description: Using Get Lost (premium removal) plus the Treasure Token to remove a 1/2 Slickshot Show-Off gives the opponent two Map tokens and delays casting Nova Hellkite by a turn (now needs 5 lands instead of having Treasure to help). While Slickshot is a real threat that can snowball with noncreature spells, spending these resources now is costly.

Targeted Momo (1/1) instead of Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant (2/2) with Burst Lightning. Sarkhan is a more dangerous engine piece that grows with +1/+1 counters whenever Dragons enter, and the opponent likely has Dragons in their deck (evidenced by Cavern of Souls). Burst Lightning can cleanly kill the 2/2 Sarkhan now, but may not be able to later if Sarkhan accumulates counters. Momo is a lesser threat that can be dealt with by smaller removal later.

The player chose to attack with only Momo (1/1 flying) instead of also attacking with Sarkhan (2/2). The opponent has no untapped creatures to block, so both Momo and Sarkhan could attack safely for 3 total damage instead of just 1. The reasoning mentions attacking with both Momo and Sarkhan, but the actual choice was only Momo. Charming Prince could also safely attack since the opponent has no blockers, making 'All attack' for 5 damage the best line. There's no reason to hold back creatures when the opponent has an empty board with no untapped mana for instant-speed interaction that would punish attacking.

Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant is a 2/2 creature that can potentially transform into a powerful dragon, but the opponent also has Momo, Friendly Flier on the battlefield. Momo is a 1/1 flier that likely provides card advantage or other synergies. However, the key issue is that Burst Lightning deals 2 damage, which kills either Sarkhan or Charming Prince equally. Sarkhan as a 2/2 planeswalker-creature is a significant threat that can transform, so targeting it is defensible. But looking at the board more carefully - the player has Lightning Helix in hand which also deals 3 damage and could kill any of these creatures. The Burst Lightning could have been used on Momo (1/1) to save the more efficient removal for the bigger threat. Using Burst Lightning (2 damage) on a 2/2 when you could use it on the 1/1 Momo and save Lightning Helix for Sarkhan (or use it to go face for the life gain) represents suboptimal resource allocation. However, Sarkhan's dragon transformation potential makes it arguably the highest priority target. The real question is whether killing Momo with Burst Lightning and Sarkhan with Lightning Helix would have been better sequencing, since Lightning Helix gains 3 life and Burst Lightning is the cheaper/less valuable removal spell being used on a higher-value target.

Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant is a planeswalker that can grow in loyalty and eventually transform into a 4/4 flying indestructible dragon - a much more dangerous threat than a vanilla 2/2 Charming Prince whose ETB already resolved. Burst Lightning's 2 damage would have exactly killed Sarkhan at 2 loyalty.

The opponent has zero creatures on board. Nova Hellkite could be cast via Warp for {2}{R}, and with 6 lands available (5 on board + Multiversal Passage in hand), both Nova Hellkite (Warp) AND Charming Prince could be cast this turn. Nova Hellkite (4/5 flying haste) entering would trigger Sarkhan (gets +1/+1 counter, becomes 3/3 flying Dragon) and Momo (gets +1/+1, becomes 2/2 flying). Attacking with all creatures into an empty board would deal approximately 11 damage (4+3+2+2), bringing opponent from 17 to 6. Instead, only Charming Prince was cast, missing enormous damage.

Cast Burst Lightning during precombat main using the only available mana, seemingly out of confusion with the interface rather than strategic intent. This wastes a burn spell that could have been more impactful later (e.g., during combat as a trick, or when Slickshot Show-Off is on the battlefield to get the +2/+0 trigger). Additionally, this leaves no mana available for any reactive plays.

message: Select cards to PUT on the BOTTOM of your library (Scry) (selected 0 of 2)
annotation_description: Player bottomed Magmatic Hellkite (a powerful Dragon that synergizes with Sarkhan) and kept Sunbillow Verge on top, despite already having Multiversal Passage in hand as their land drop for this turn. With 5 lands after playing Passage, they can already cast Nova Hellkite next turn. The 6th land is redundant while a second Dragon would provide additional pressure and trigger Sarkhan's +1/+1 counter ability.

Burst Lightning deals 2 damage, which doesn't kill Sarkhan (a 2/2 with 2 toughness) — wait, it does kill a 2-toughness creature. However, targeting Sarkhan over Momo is debatable. Momo, Friendly Flier reduces the cost of the opponent's flying creatures by {1} and pumps when flying creatures enter. Given that the opponent appears to be playing a Boros fliers/dragons deck with Sarkhan and potentially Nova Hellkites, Momo's cost reduction is very relevant. Sarkhan needs a Dragon to behold to create treasure and only gets counters when Dragons enter - it's a 2/2 that doesn't do much without Dragons on board. Meanwhile, Momo is enabling cheaper threats every turn. That said, Sarkhan's scaling potential with Dragons is real, making this a close call.

Targeted Charming Prince (a vanilla 2/2 after its ETB) instead of Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant, which is a much more dangerous threat. Sarkhan grows with +1/+1 counters whenever Dragons enter and creates Treasure tokens, and can snowball rapidly. Charming Prince's value was already extracted on ETB.

Casting Lightning Helix to face before deploying Slickshot Show-Off wastes a potential +2/+0 pump trigger. At 12 life, the 3 life gain is relevant, but plotting Slickshot Show-Off this turn (1R) would set up a much more powerful future turn where Slickshot comes down for free and gets pumped by multiple burn spells (Lightning Helix + 2x Burst Lightning). The opponent's board is mostly tapped, so there's no immediate pressure requiring the life gain this turn.

Targeting opponent's face with Lightning Helix while behind on board at 12 life. Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant is a high-priority removal target that can transform into a powerful dragon. While the 6-point life swing (17→14 opponent, 12→15 self) helps racing, the opponent has multiple creatures applying pressure.

Targeted Charming Prince (a vanilla 2/2 with its ETB already used) with Burst Lightning instead of Sarkhan, Dragon Ascendant, which is a much more dangerous card that can transform into a 4/4 flying dragon and enables dragon synergies.

chosen_display: Map Token — {1}, {T}, Sacrifice this artifact: Target creatur... [Activate]
annotation_description: Player incorrectly stated they have no creatures on the battlefield to target with Map Token's explore ability, but they have Slickshot Show-Off in play. Activating a Map Token before combat would let Slickshot Show-Off explore, potentially gaining a +1/+1 counter (making it a 2/3 flyer for combat) or drawing a useful card. This was pure upside that was declined based on a misread of the board.

Player declined to activate Map Token, incorrectly believing they had no creatures to target. Slickshot Show-Off was on the battlefield and could have been targeted to explore. With only 3 lands on turn 5 and two Nova Hellkites (5-mana) in hand, exploring to potentially find a land was extremely valuable. Even hitting a non-land (putting a +1/+1 counter on Slickshot and filtering the bottom of the library) would have been pure upside.

Casting Burst Lightning during precombat main without a clear strategic target. With only Rockface Village untapped (which produces R only for creatures), the mana situation is questionable. More importantly, using Burst Lightning proactively here wastes a removal/burn spell that could answer future threats like Nova Hellkite from the opponent or be saved for a lethal burn sequence. The AI's own reasoning admits it's casting 'to break a loop' rather than for strategic value.

Burst Lightning deals 2 damage and was targeted at the opponent's face (13 life -> 11 life) instead of killing Momo, Friendly Flier (1/1), a key synergy piece that reduces costs for flying creatures and gets pumped whenever flying creatures enter. Momo enables the opponent's Dragon/flying strategy by making their threats cheaper and growing itself. Removing Momo for just 2 damage is far more impactful than dealing 2 to face when the opponent is at 13 life and there's no realistic burn-them-out line visible (opponent has Sacred Foundry untapped and Get Lost/Lightning Helix-style interaction available). The 2 face damage is largely irrelevant at this life total, while Momo continuing to provide cost reduction and grow could be very relevant.

Player incorrectly believed they couldn't activate Map Token, but Rockface Village can tap for {C} which pays the {1} generic cost. Activating a Map Token to explore with Slickshot Show-Off (currently pumped to 7/2 from three noncreature spells) could yield a +1/+1 counter for 1 extra damage (8/3 attacking), or find a land card. At 2 life in a race situation, every point of damage and card selection matters.

Gem25F Analyst has Rockface Village untapped which can produce {C}, sufficient to pay the {1} activation cost of a Map Token. At 2 life vs opponent's 3 life, exploring Slickshot Show-Off could find a burn spell or put a +1/+1 counter on it, which could be the difference between winning and losing. The Map Tokens are sorcery-speed only, so this postcombat main phase is the correct window.
